name: ERock (Enchanted Rock)
employees: ~300-315 (May 2026, aggregator-reported; not confirmed in the S-1)

ownership.notes: IPO'd June 10, 2026 at $21.50/share (27.9M Class A shares, ~$600M gross; Morgan Stanley/J.P. Morgan leads). UP-C structure over Enchanted Rock Holdings, LLC: public float ~10.2% of economics / ~12.7% of votes. Energy Impact Partners is the largest pre-IPO institutional owner (entities tied to EIP's Hans Kobler hold ~83.4M Class B + ~19.4M Class A); founder Thomas McAndrew retains a disclosed ~31.9% beneficial stake. Tax Receivable Agreement obligates up to ~$1.19B of undiscounted payments to pre-IPO owners. Historic fleet capex ran off-balance-sheet through Basalt Infrastructure Partners' Texas Microgrid LLC vehicle.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: ERock (rebranded from Enchanted Rock at its June 2026 NYSE IPO) is the most bankable pure-play in the FEOC-immune gas-microgrid category that is siphoning AIDC energy budgets away from grid-plus-BESS architectures. Three anchor contracts define it: Microsoft San Jose (100 MW RNG-backed backup, complete), Meta El Paso via El Paso Electric (McCloud Generation — 366 MW, ~$473-500M, utility-owned and Meta-funded, exclusive 5-year bridge from 2027, construction started Q2 2026), and an ~470 MW RockBlock equipment order from Anthropic (August 11, 2026 — its largest ever, taking backlog to ~$1.7B, 10x year-over-year, and moving the stock +23%). The platform is pure natural-gas gensets — 500 kW ERT500 units and megawatt-scale RockBlock strings assembled in Houston-area plants ramping toward ~1.2 GW/yr by end-2026 at only ~$15M capex — with zero BESS in the product line. For Hithium the company is not a battery rival but a demand-shaper: every campus that signs an ERock bridge defers or shrinks a containerized-storage purchase, while ERock's own post-bridge narrative ('permanent utility feeds supplemented by battery storage') and its ex-Stem CEO leave a visible storage-attach socket open.
ecosystemRole: We assess ERock as the archetype of the FEOC-immune energy dollar in US AIDC — a public, cash-rich ($626.6M, zero debt), vertically integrated gas-genset platform selling bridge power, diesel-replacement backup, and flexible-capacity interconnection enablement to exactly the hyperscaler budgets a containerized BESS supplier targets. It competes with VoltaGrid and ProEnergy inside the gas-bridge category, competes with grid-plus-BESS at the architecture level, and — because its own roadmap concedes battery supplementation after the bridge years — doubles as a plausible future BESS procurement channel that Hithium's NDAA §154 designation likely locks it out of on US soil.

productsAndServices.name: RockBlock + ERT500 modular gas gensets (the AIDC product)
productsAndServices.description: Launched September 2025: ERT500 is a 500 kW modular natural-gas genset; RockBlock is the megawatt-scale 'diesel replacement' — modular strings of 1.5-3.5 MW configurable in 0.5 MW increments. Legacy fleet built on ~0.45 MW units (Microsoft San Jose runs 224 of them). Engines are Power Solutions International 21.9L natural-gas blocks (400 kWe LTR / 448 kWe standby) under a ~$335M mutually exclusive five-year supply agreement — PSI is majority-owned by China's Weichai Power, an under-discussed supply-chain irony inside the 'FEOC-clean' pitch. Marketed against diesel: up to 99% fewer particulates, no water use, <70 dBA, unlimited pipeline-fed runtime, ~20-year life, avoids Title V major-source permitting; CARB DG-compliant.
productsAndServices.positioning: Direct competitor to diesel backup (Cat/Cummins/MTU) on emissions and grid value, to VoltaGrid and ProEnergy on AIDC bridge power (smaller unit granularity, deeper utility integration), and to grid-plus-BESS at the architecture level. Not a BESS product — batteries appear only at the edges (software dispatch of third-party storage, hybrid Texas Backup Power Package configs, post-bridge storage narrative).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Three routes: (1) reliability-as-a-service — customer pays a service fee, ERock monetizes the fleet in ERCOT as an aggregated VPP; (2) straight equipment sales with ~10-year O&M attach (>95% attach, 100% renewal, $23.6M annualized recurring service revenue); (3) utility-partner program — utilities (Entergy 'Power Through', ComEd, El Paso Electric) own or resell the microgrid service.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscale and AI data centers (bridge, backup, flexible capacity), utilities, C&I resiliency (H-E-B, Walmart, Buc-ee's), municipal water infrastructure
productsAndServices.roadmap: Production 'completely sold out through 2027 and into 2028' (Q2 2026 call); Hyperion assembly plant (Cypress, TX) began operations Q2 2026 targeting ~1.2 GW/yr by end-2026; HyBLOX hydrogen-blend engine program ($2.1M CEC grant); RNG supply flowing to Microsoft San Jose from early 2026 via US Energy food-waste partnership.

productsAndServices.name: Bridge-to-grid and flexible-capacity structures
productsAndServices.description: Productized May 2024 explicitly for AI-driven load: prime power ahead of interconnection (the Meta El Paso template — utility-owned, hyperscaler-funded, exclusive 5-year bridge), diesel-replacement backup (Microsoft), and 'flexible capacity' that lets a campus accept non-firm/curtailable interconnection for faster grid access — the same enablement role 4-hour BESS plays in competing architectures.
productsAndServices.positioning: The El Paso Electric/McCloud structure — a $473-500M plant owned by the utility, fully paid by Meta under a commission-approved rate, operated by ERock — is the template competitors now have to answer; it converts a merchant bridge sale into regulated-utility paper.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility rate filings (PUCT), direct hyperscaler equipment POs (Anthropic), RaaS contracts
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscalers with stranded interconnection queues; utilities monetizing large-load connection demand
productsAndServices.roadmap: McCloud construction started Q2 2026, bridge service from 2027; Anthropic 470 MW extends production commitments into 2028 with O&M contracts to follow separately.

productsAndServices.name: GraniteEcosystem software + ERCOT VPP operations
productsAndServices.description: Monitoring, predictive analytics, and automated dispatch that forecasts market/grid conditions and optimizes onsite generation, solar, storage and other resources. The founding economic thesis: aggregated microgrids sell energy and ancillary services into ERCOT, and that wholesale revenue subsidizes the customer's resiliency fee (dual-value). Historically monetized through Basalt's Texas Microgrid LLC (~167-225 MW).
productsAndServices.positioning: The software layer is the one place ERock's architecture formally touches batteries today — GraniteEcosystem can dispatch third-party storage in hybrid microgrids, and the Texas Backup Power Package ($1.8B, ≤2.5 MW projects at $500/kW) requires solar+battery+gas combinations.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with RaaS and O&M contracts
productsAndServices.targetSegments: All fleet customers; Texas program participants
productsAndServices.roadmap: Watch for storage-attach productization — CEO John Carrington ran Stem, Inc. (BESS/AI software) and the bridge narrative concedes post-bridge battery supplementation.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess ERock as a demand-shaper, not a battery competitor: every AIDC campus that signs an ERock bridge or backup contract defers, shrinks, or eliminates a containerized BESS purchase for that phase of the buildout. The three anchor deals (Microsoft, Meta/EPE, Anthropic) represent ~936 MW of gas capacity serving loads that grid-plus-BESS architectures would otherwise have addressed.

(High confidence) The FEOC-immunity of the platform is central to its momentum — hyperscalers can buy 470 MW of it with zero sourcing-compliance diligence, in direct contrast to Chinese-cell BESS after the Jan 2026 Section 301 escalation and FY2026 NDAA §154-type prohibitions. The irony we would keep in reserve: ERock's single-source engine supplier PSI is majority-owned by China's Weichai Power, so the 'clean' supply chain has its own China dependency one layer down.

(Medium confidence) The storage-attach socket is real and dated: ERock's own bridge narrative concedes sites transition to 'permanent utility feeds supplemented by battery storage' after the ~5-year bridge, GraniteEcosystem already dispatches third-party storage, the Texas Backup Power Package forces solar+battery+gas hybrids, and the CEO is the former CEO of Stem. We expect a formal storage offering or partnership within 24 months — and Hithium's §154 designation makes it a near-certain design-out on US soil, while the structure itself (utility-owned, hyperscaler-funded) is the template Hithium's US customers will face.

(Medium confidence) Customer concentration is the principal fragility: three contracts dominate the growth story, sell-side now frames the stock as an Anthropic derivative, and the $1.7B backlog must convert through an assembly ramp (Hyperion) that has never run at rate. A slip in H2 2026 deliveries would re-break the stock and slow the category's momentum — a window in which BESS-based architectures regain relative bankability.

(Low confidence) Emissions friction is the sleeper risk to the whole gas-bridge category: BAAQMD objected to run-hour assumptions at Microsoft San Jose, El Paso council scrutiny targets NOx/CO from 813 engines, and EPA tightening on long-duration 'mobile' generation would raise costs across ERock, VoltaGrid, and ProEnergy simultaneously — the scenario in which BESS attach accelerates fastest.
